bullets.text: ML is a subfield of AI focused on systems learning from data without explicit programming.
Core idea: systems learn patterns and make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Used in image recognition, natural language processing, predictive analytics, and autonomous vehicles.
Growth driven by large datasets, improved computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Supervised Learning: Trained on labeled data to predict known outputs (e.g., regression, classification).
Unsupervised Learning: Trained on unlabeled data to find hidden patterns (e.g., clustering, dimensionality reduction).
Reinforcement Learning: Agent learns by interacting with an environment to maximize rewards (e.g., robotics, gaming).
Model Training: Feeding data to a model to learn patterns and adjust parameters.
Features and Labels: Input variables (features) and target outputs (labels) in supervised learning.
Training and Testing Sets: Data split for model training and performance evaluation.
Overfitting: Model learns training data too well, performs poorly on new data.
Underfitting: Model is too simple and fails to capture important data patterns.
Linear Regression: Models linear relationships for continuous output prediction.
Logistic Regression: Predicts probability of belonging to a class for classification tasks.
Decision Trees: Non-linear model splitting data into subsets for decision-making.
Random Forest: Ensemble method combining multiple decision trees for improved performance.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): Finds optimal hyperplane to separate data points for classification.
Neural Networks: Inspired by the human brain, learns complex patterns for deep learning applications.
Healthcare: Disease diagnosis, drug discovery, personalized treatment.
Finance: Fraud detection, credit scoring, algorithmic trading.
Marketing: Customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: Processing sensor data, decision-making, safe navigation.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): Language translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization.
Training and Testing: Assess performance using separate datasets with metrics like accuracy, MSE.
Cross-Validation: Technique to ensure model generalizes well to unseen data.
Hyperparameter Tuning: Optimizing model settings for optimal performance (e.g., grid search).
Data Quality and Quantity: Requires large amounts of accurate, consistent data; labeled data collection can be hard.
Interpretability: Complex models (deep learning) are often difficult to understand.
Bias in Data: Models can inherit biases from training data, leading to unfair outcomes.
Overfitting and Underfitting: Common issues impacting model generalization.
Continuous evolution with advancements in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI (XAI).
Increased computational power and datasets will expand ML's role across industries.
ML applications will become more integrated into daily life.
Ethical considerations and responsible AI practices are crucial for progress.
